⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • OUR FITNESS EDITORS love to slip on cushy sneakers like the Hoka Clifton 11 for our 5Ks and hot girl walks.
  • “They’re designed to handle side-to-side movement, quick pivots, and changes in direction—not just forward motion,” indicates Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

OUR FITNESS EDITORS love to slip on cushy sneakers like the Hoka Clifton 11 for our 5Ks and hot girl walks. But on days when we're lifting heavy, doing a functional strength training workout, or have a gym sesh that switches between lifts and sprints, we turn to our favorite cross-training shoes. If you’re unfamiliar with the term, cross-training is combining different exercise modalities—like cardio, resistance training, and plyometric (rapid movements)—during a gym session. Think of these sneakers as multipurpose powerhouses. They keep your feet locked in, whether you’re deadlifting or speed walking on an under-desk treadmill.

“They’re designed to handle side-to-side movement, quick pivots, and changes in direction—not just forward motion,” indicates Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois. “This makes them more supportive for gym workouts, classes, or sports where your foot needs stability in multiple planes, like pickleball or tennis.” On the flip side, a walking or running shoe usually only supports you in straight-line motion, Lockwood says.

It has been revealed that wearing running sneakers for strength training workouts is generally a no-no (except for the caveat about the Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 below). All the podiatrists I spoke with say it’s safer and beneficial to invest in cross-training shoes. That’s because they usually have flatter outsoles and thinner midsoles than running shoes to keep your feet locked in, says Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California. That way, you won’t wobble during your deadlifts and box jumps. The material of cross-training shoes is also more durable than running shoes to resist wear and tear, and has thick heel counters to help prevent ankle injuries.

Whether you're a seasoned weightlifting junkie or a runner on a mission to integrate more training modalities into your routine, read on for the best cross-training shoes you can find.

After testing dozens of cross-training shoes this past year, the latest lululemon Chargefeel 3 stands out for its impeccable support and stability during speedy, lateral movements like ice skaters, kettlebell squats, and Zumba workouts. We’ve been fans of the Chargefeel line for years, with the previous edition—the Chargefeel 2—winning the best cross-training shoe for our 2025 WH Sneaker Awards. Lululemon has since made a few tweaks that make it even better. “Despite the fact that sneaker fit and feel is extremely subjective, everyone I know who has worked out in the Chargefeel—myself included—has loved its perfect balance of stability and flexibility,” says WH executive health and fitness director Jacqueline Andriakos, NASM-CPT.

It’s now 8 ounces instead of 9.1 ounces, and has a lower heel-to-toe drop—6 mm compared to 9.5 mm—to help alleviate stress on the ankles and feet. WH associate style and commerce editor Shannen Zitz loves the wider build for lifting and squatting. She indicates her feet feel locked in and extra secure. “My feet stay securely in place thanks to a forefoot-hugging band on the inside of the shoe and a tough plastic heel counter,” says Zitz. She also notes that the springy EVA foam cushioning makes it a workhorse for walking and running.

Sources indicate that and post-workout, it’s a great leisure kick for traveling or running errands. “I recently wore these while traveling, and they kept my feet super happy power walking through the airport and standing on long security and customs lines,” Zitz adds. Andriakos agrees, stating, “The stylish silhouette looks good outside the gym.”.

Sources indicate that the fit is true to size, and the breathable knit upper doesn’t feel constricting when wearing thick socks (perfect for combating blisters!). Although wide size options are not available, the toes still have adequate room to spread with each step or lift. However, Zitz notes the wide outsole may feel too bulky during quick and dynamic HIIT workouts.

Read More: Every Lululemon Shoe, Ranked.

We wouldn’t recommend most running shoes for cross-training, but the Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 is an exception. You can effortlessly transition from long runs to deadlifts, thanks to its balanced cushioning and moderate heel-to-toe drop.

According to recent reports, compared to the GTS 24, the latest version has slightly softer cushioning, with about 3 mm more foam in the forefoot and 1 mm in the heel, giving it a smoother, more comfortable feel underfoot. It also drops from 12 mm to 10 mm, creating a slightly more level feel. That can make it feel more stable during strength work than higher-drop running shoes.

It has been revealed that at 9 ounces, it’s a lightweight gem, especially for those with overpronation or flat feet during agility drills. Its GuideRails technology—firm foam on both sides of the foot—keeps feet aligned during everything from Bulgarian split squats to lunges to speed walking. Plus, stiff heel padding keeps feet from sliding."These feel super comfortable and supportive for everyday life, traditional workouts, walks, easy runs—you name it," claims Melissa Kendter, CPT, a functional strength coach. "I love that this shoe feels well cushioned but doesn't have a huge chunky sole, making it more appropriate for strength workouts than most running shoes.".

According to recent reports, because the outsole is relatively smooth (it’s built for road miles, not side-to-side gym moves), we’d stick to non-slip floors for quick lateral work. If your workouts are heavy on lifting or plyometrics, a flatter cross-trainer like the Nike Metcon 10 may feel steadier and more secure underfoot.

Read More: Brooks Adrenaline GTS 25 Review.

In a recent development, we’ve been fans of the Nano series since 2018, and every year we notice Reebok levels up its cushioning and heel stability to keep our feet locked in and comfortable during even the most intense workouts. The midsole padding is firm for balancing during heavy lifts and lateral movements, yet is still bouncy for excellent rebound during HIIT workouts and explosive jumps. The mesh material upper is also firm, keeping you steady when lifting heavy.

MH digital designer Taryn Colbert used to prefer flat lifestyle shoes like Converse or Vans, but has since switched over to the Nano X5 for her cross-training sessions. The stiffer soles offer her better balance, while she notes that the heel counter is dense, meaning it doesn’t flex easily. However, the 7 mm heel-to-toe drop may be too steep for some weightlifters who prefer a ground-feel shoe. But it’s a pro if you like extra heel support.

In a recent development, the grippy outsole delivers superior traction when executing deadlifts or weighted squats, while the snug laces never budge. Colbert also notes that the breathable material helps combat sweaty feet. Just note that the fit runs tight (consider ordering at least a half-size up), and it weighs 12.1 ounces, making it one of the heaviest shoes in this guide.

If your workouts focus on dynamic moves like kettlebell swings or heavy lifting, the Nobull Drive is a gem. It’s crafted with a breathable mesh knit upper that feels sock-like and keeps feet cool during grueling reps.

The balance of flexibility and firmness makes it simple to transition from the squat rack to the HIIT studio. WH associate editor Olivia Luppino wears them during physical therapy to help maintain balance when doing Bosu ball squats, and then hits the gym to do deadlifts. She also notes the mesh isn’t scratchy—an issue she has had when wearing this material.

Sources indicate that the subtle foam feels similar to a minimally-cushioned running shoe, while the low 4 mm drop keeps Luppino grounded when deadlifting. She also notes that a firm heel counter makes her feet feel secure without too much stiffness. And at 8.3 ounces, it’s the lightest shoe in this guide, which makes it an optimal choice for sprints and mixed-modality workouts.

In a recent development, nike’s latest Metcon 10 is a top pick among our editors when it comes to pumping iron. Its main enhancement compared to the last iteration is a smaller, stiffer plate strategically placed under the heel to help stabilize the feet when squatting heavy reps or doing deadlifts. It’s also lighter at 11.8 ounces (it was previously 13.3 ounces) and feels more responsive during jumps and HIIT when it’s not leg day.

Industry observers note that zitz was completely sold after her first wear. “I feel totally grounded with the 4 mm drop while squatting and lunging, and they never weigh me down while running,” notes Zitz. “I also love how sleek and stylish they look (especially in the pink color!), and I've been wearing them with nearly every athleisure fit since I got them.”.

Sources indicate that the tough rubber traction is another highlight. It feels almost sticky, helping you stay put. Zitz adds that the grooves on the outsole are great for slick sidewalks or dynamic movements, like box jumps. The mesh upper also offers some breathability, but it’s not the most airy shoe in this guide.

Read More: Best Weightlifting Shoes.

The RAD One V2 is so flexible that it feels like an extension of your feet during lifts, drills, and cardio. The forefoot bends easily and delivers bounce that feels natural. Accardi notes her movement feels “controlled, yet free” when these are on her feet. “While firmness is important in a cross-training shoe, many are too stiff, which limits power in workouts unrelated to lifting,” she says. “These feel nimble yet stable for agility drills and plyometric moves like box jumps.”.

Sources indicate that the moderate 6 mm drop and heel counter provide balance and sturdiness. The springy EVA midsole also alleviates joint impact during high-impact moves. And bonus: the cushioning is wrapped with rubber to help combat wear and tear, while the textured outsole provides perfect traction during lateral bounds and tuck jumps. “My footing feels nice and steady during transitions, whether I’m going fast or slow.”.

Recent findings suggest that note that this kick is the heaviest option in this guide, weighing 12.8 ounces. It’s not the best option for long-distance runs, but it’s a top pick if you’re all about explosive movements.

On is a cult-fave among runners for its cloud-like outsole that’s become a style statement, but the Cloudpulse Pro proves the brand is also a game changer in cross-training shoes. Besides short sprints, it’s designed for workouts that blend cardio and strength—box jumps, sprints, step-ups, and ice skaters. Its signature CloudTec cushioning—compressive foam that absorbs impact—is ultra-bouncy and makes you feel like you’re flying during jumps and agility drills. It propels you forward whether you’re walking, running, or doing dynamic movements. One word that describes it perfectly is energetic. The foam also isn’t overly soft, which is great for support during fast transitions.

Sources indicate that the 6 mm heel-to-toe drop keeps Accardi grounded and balanced during lateral and dynamic movements. A firm heel counter keeps her feet secure, which gives her the confidence to grind hard. Weighing 10.6 ounces, it feels resilient yet solid. The thick, grippy outsole also helps her maintain control on smooth, slick floors. Plus, the polyester material evaporates sweat to keep feet dry.

The fit is roomy, especially in the toe box, making it an excellent option for those with wide feet or bunions. “The fit is perfection,” notes WH food producer Tina Martinez. “It’s streamlined through the narrowest part of my foot and hugs my arches in the most secure way.”.

Read More: Best On Shoes for Walking.

Sources indicate that if you want a marshmallow-like feel in your cross-training kicks, the While On Earth Move Trainer is a star pick that’s plush minus the bulk. The spongy EVA foam is ideal for short or long runs, while a heel counter (hard plastic that wraps around the heel) prevents any budging during weight training. It’s also light and nimble at 10.6 ounces, making it a workhorse for cardio and strength work.

WH deputy visual editor Dangi McCoy says it’s super supportive during at-home workouts and lateral movements like lunges and shuffling. Plus, it requires no break-in period before hitting the gym. “The width of the shoe itself is great for stability—my feet and toes are secure with any movement,” says McCoy. The wide base and toe box offer ample space for natural foot movement, especially during fast circuit training and intervals, while the neutral 6 mm drop promotes even landings.

It has been revealed that another nice feature: It’s stain and water-resistant. While this shoe is comfortable enough for running, the Brooks Adrenaline GTS 24 is better for long runs. But sprints and short-distance running workouts? For sure.

Weekly cross-training puts wear and tear on your shoes, so picking a durable pair is a priority. The GORUCK Ballistic Trainer is strong and resilient enough to handle demanding training from plyometrics to climbing. The Cordura nylon upper is abrasion-resistant and strong, while the rubber outsole is thick and sturdy to sustain repetitive force. Accardi has even worn it to rock climb. “The fabric still looks like it did straight out of the box after scraping against a climbing wall,” says Accardi. “The sole also kept me from slipping on challenging areas.”.

The 8 mm drop feels level, making it practical for barbell squats or deadlifts, while the EVA foam midsole is plush enough to absorb impact during sprints and jumps. And don’t worry—it doesn’t skimp on stability. A heel counter secures the feet to the insole during weight-bearing exercises. As for fit, a wide toe box allows for comfy movement.

Nike took the best traits of its iconic Free running shoe to create the Metcon 6—a trusty hybrid running and cross trainer. Whether you’re executing agility drills, speed work, or lunges, it delivers the perfect combination of comfort and stability, no matter what workout you have on deck. "This is perfect for my training workouts that consist of part speed run intervals and part strength training because of its combination of cushioning and stability," says Ashley Barnett, NASM-CPT. She adds that it’s great for jumping, strength routines, and mixed workouts. Accardi also loves wearing it during HIIT classes, highlighting its flexibility and responsiveness when transitioning from burpees to high knees.

Compared to the Metcon 10, it has a higher drop at 7.2 mm. While this is a pro in a running shoe, it may mean having less stability during heavy lifts. It’s also worth noting that it fits snug and narrow, so you may have to go up a half size. Accardi has bunions and had to size up to prevent the fabric from rubbing against the sides of her feet during runs and agility drills.

According to recent reports, everyone has a unique foot shape, and each brand can fit differently. So, finding the right fit can be complex. But as a general rule of thumb, your feet should feel supported, not suffocated, and you shouldn't be counting down the minutes until you can kick them off, says Mali Pelham, CPT, C.F.S.C., a personal trainer at Wattage in Chicago.

An easy way to measure if you have enough space is by being able to slide your finger back and forth at the back of the heel. Also, your shoes shouldn’t feel like they’re pinching the middle of your foot—this can lead to tingling and numbness if they’re too tight. If you’re completely unsure, it doesn’t hurt to get fitted at a shoe store. Referencing brands’ sizing charts can also be helpful. Also, pay attention to width, as different brands offer narrow and wide options.

Heel-to-toe drop refers to the height difference between the heel and the forefoot of the shoe.

Consider the type of workouts you'll be tackling in your latest kicks. Each demands specific qualities in a shoe, though the best cross-training shoes for women are versatile enough to let you do all these workouts in them.

The Women’s Health team has spent almost seven years (since 2018!) testing and curating the ultimate guide to the best cross-training shoes for women by putting more than 50 cross-training shoes through their paces. Our rigorous testing process involved multiple phases, including scouring reviews, consulting industry experts, and most importantly, testing the shoes firsthand. We laced up cross-trainers for a battery of tests designed to assess performance across various activities, including weightlifting, cardio, agility drills, and CrossFit workouts. Then, we evaluated whether or not a shoe is functional for different kinds of workouts, has enough stability to prevent ankle rolling, is durable enough to withstand wear and tear, and is comfortable for long hours at the gym. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, your electric vehicle battery may last longer than you think.
  • The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.
  • Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, your electric vehicle battery may last longer than you think. Ford indicates its EV batteries retain greater than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. Here are a few tips to keep yours healthy.

The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.

Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.

According to Ford, the Mach-E’s battery has retained 92% of its health on average over the past five years.

Across its full EV lineup, including the F-150 Lightning and E-Transit, Ford noted its battery packs maintain more than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. The key number to look at is the spread, with 95% of vehicles falling between 87% and 97% health.

Of 2021 model-year EV owners, Ford remarked, more than 2,000 have crossed 100,000 miles with their original battery averaging better than 91% health, while over 30 have crossed the 200,000-mile mark and average 88% health.

Ford is using real-world data to help owners take good care of their electric vehicles, no matter how much they know about batteries and other EV tech.

It’s also applying lessons from developing the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, which will underpin its next-generation EVs, starting with the Fantom pickup next year.

According to recent reports, ford offered a few simple, everyday tips to help owners support long-term battery health. For one, if possible, charge at home on Level 2 for daily commuting or driving and save DC fast charging for longer trips.

Industry observers note that it also helps to avoid charging in extreme temperatures if you can. Preconditioning the battery can help bring it into the optimal temperature range, while parking in the shade on hot summer days can also help avoid long-term battery degradation.

Last, but not least, you can use the Ford App to find charge-level recommendations designed specifically for your vehicle and battery system.

The 2021 Mustang Mach-E uses an NCM battery, but some newer Ford batteries use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery chemistry, which is recommended to charge to 100% from time to time.

Ford has introduced new features in the Ford App to help owners maintain battery health specific to their vehicle and will continue to use the data to improve the experience as it introduces its next-gen EVs.

This is an article about Ford EV's, so my comment is kind of relevant.

According to recent reports, recently I picked up a 2017 Ford Focus Electric for my daughter to use when she gets her permit soon. It had 91,000 miles when I got it and now has 92,400 miles. I like driving it enough that I've been driving it and letting my Equinox stay home.

It has been revealed that now, I have no idea how this car has been used or charged since fresh (does have the DCFC since it's a 2017). And since it's range was 115 miles factory rated, I have no idea if it's been charged to 100% most or all of the time. What I can tell you is that when I charge it to 100% now, it's giving me about 120 miles on average and I've seen as high as 134 miles. If I turn the A/C on, those numbers drop to 110 on average. Since I live in a mild climate and use the A/C sparingly, my daily commute with mixed driving is giving me a real life 120 to 125 miles.

Not bad for a nearly 10 years old compliance EV!!

Ford will open pre-orders for the Fathom, a midsize electric pickup and first UEV-based model, starting at $28,350 in early 2027.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E is now on sale, starting at $39,995. The 2027 Mach-E drops the standard-range battery offered in the 2026 model and now comes standard with the larger 88 kWh battery with an EPA-estimated range of up to 320 miles (RWD).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The most wonderful time of the year holds a special place in Jordyn Woods-Towns’s heart—and no, we’re not talking about the start of basketball season. The fashion designer got engaged to Knicks phenom Karl-Anthony Towns on Christmas Eve 2025, and after a whirlwind 2026 including an NBA championship win for the New York NBA team (possibly courtesy of her viral accessory-turned-amulet) and a clifftop wedding replete with stunning details, the couple can’t wait to create festive memories as husband and wife.

According to recent reports, “This is my first married Christmas,” Woods-Town tells AD. “I’ve only been married three months, but it’s our first holiday season, so I definitely need to try to figure out what our new traditions are.”.

The newlywed reveals that she created an entire PowerPoint presentation to prep attendees for her bachelorette party, so you’d best believe she appreciates a little organization when it comes to getting in the spirit for big days. Planner that she is, Woods-Towns linked up with design marketplace Minted for her first family Christmas card and a curated suite of picks to welcome one particularly merry and bright yuletide season of life. Below, AD gets her take on holiday colors, basketball-themed decor, and more.

In anticipation of the holiday season, Woods-Towns teamed up with Minted to curate a selection of festive stationery and decor.

Architectural Digest: Have you always been a substantial holiday person?

Jordyn Woods-Towns: Every single season, I decorate. On Valentine’s Day I have the girls over to do a charcuterie board with salami roses and chocolate covered strawberries. Karl and I went crazy for Halloween; we turned the entire front yard into a whole different space with a graveyard and a 20-foot-tall skeleton. On Christmas, I love a theme.

It has been revealed that for a couple years I went with a Candy Cane Lane vibe and now I’m in my chic New York era. I love a Ralph Lauren Christmas. I love the natural linen and natural materials. I’ve been really into natural florals, textural things. I love feathers, incorporating some ostrich feathers throughout—I do a lot of that with my brand, and I feel like feathers are really having a moment right now.

In Newly introduced York it’s been hard because I don’t drive and I don’t have my car. I can’t just run down to HomeGoods, grab something, and come back!

What’s your decor looking like this year?

I’ve been really into all one shade. There were a lot of greens in our wedding and green is my color of the season.

Woods-Towns is leaning toward florals and green for holiday decorating this year.

So it’s a green Christmas this year?

The tree’s already green. It could be kind of cool, full green-on-green. Now I’m the Grinch. [laughs].

According to recent reports, with your Christmas Eve engagement last year, the holiday is a sweet part of your love story. What sorts of traditions are you looking forward to starting with Karl?

Recent findings suggest that I started with the holiday card with Minted. This is our first holiday card as a family. Obviously after you have kids, it kind of changes, but right now we’re at a time where life is just… he has a [Christmas Day] game and so we’re like, “Okay, we’re living the young, fast life.” But as time goes on, as our marriage goes on, we’re going to build different traditions. We love to be with our family and I always cook every holiday, so I’ll definitely be cooking after the game.

Is there a signature dish you like to serve?

Recent findings suggest that karl’s a picky eater. He loves chicken, so some version of chicken. He’s never had beef or pork or anything in his whole entire life. It’s just us, so some type of chicken and sides. Pretty simple.

What was the vibe of your holiday card?

I wanted to use a photo from our wedding that really felt like us, something that not everyone has seen, to tie in our whole year. It was a green marbled border design with gold foil border by Jenna Holcomb. There are those shades of green, since there’s a lot of green incorporated into our wedding. Olive is very timeless, and it felt chic and like us, like something that people could keep. I don’t want to say everyone’s going to want to put a photo of us in their house, but I know our family [will].

The Towns family’s holiday card. The design is “Marbled” by Jenna Holcomb.

Are you hosting bigger parties this season or just keeping it more intimate with the celebrations?

No huge parties, just because I don’t have the capacity to do that right now, but definitely getting the family together. We don’t have a huge family, so it should be pretty intimate, hopefully doing something with the team getting together. I think one of the girls was talking about doing a holiday party—even though I love to be the host, I don’t mind just showing up.

Recent findings suggest that I would say it’s all in the details. I think through everything. But overall, it’s about the vibe that you’re bringing, the energy, and what you’re putting out. People remember the music, the food, and how they felt.

It’s been a busy 2026 for Woods-Towns between then-fiancé Karl-Anthony Towns’s successful championship run with the New York Knicks and her August wedding, but she’s keeping her energy high heading into holiday party season. “I feel like there’s an event every other day. But it’s not going to be like this forever. I had to change my mindset from, ‘Wow, I’m so tired,’ to, ‘Wow, I’m so lucky to be able to do this.’”.

Are you planning on sprinkling any Knicks Easter eggs throughout your home decor or in your gifting this year?

In a recent development, there’s so many Knicks things in my house that it’s hard to escape. It’s already everywhere, the whole house is Knicks-ed out already! But I don’t mind Knicks-themed gifting—people love the Knicks.

Recent findings suggest that karl’s very hard to gift for, and his birthday’s actually right before the holidays. So it’s hard to figure out two really good gifts in a short amount of time. Gift giving is one of my love languages, and I love getting people things that they really can utilize in their everyday life. I need to think about that.

How else do you get in the holiday spirit at home?

I already bought Christmas pajamas and I already watched The Grinch twice with my niece and nephew two days ago. So I’m ready!

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention.
  • But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.
  • According to recent reports, unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention. That’s sort of the point. They look like Vespas, ride like Vespas, and just happen to swap the gasoline engine for a much quieter electric drivetrain.

But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.

According to recent reports, unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica. And while you’d be forgiven for struggling to spot the differences from across the show floor, there’s a lot more happening underneath.

It has been revealed that the biggest upgrade is an entirely new electric motor developed and manufactured in Italy by Vespa parent organization Piaggio Group. The motor uses a new modular design intended to improve both performance and efficiency, while also doing away with rare-earth materials.

On the 45 km/h (28 mph) Primavera and Sprint S models, Vespa states the new motor provides stronger acceleration for stop-and-go city riding. Range reaches up to 85 km (53 miles) in Eco mode.

According to recent reports, but perhaps the biggest practical improvement is the fresh removable battery. Being able to pull the battery out of the scooter and carry it inside for charging makes a massive difference for urban riders who don’t have access to a garage or dedicated charging spot – exactly the kind of riders Vespa is targeting.

It has been revealed that the Primavera Tech is where things get a little faster. This version is homologated as a motorcycle rather than a moped in Europe and reaches 67 km/h (42 mph). That’s still not terribly fast, but the electric Vespa line has never been known for its top speed.

Its range has increased by 12.5% thanks to the newly introduced motor and Vehicle Management System, reaching 90 km (56 miles) on the WMTC cycle or up to 100 km (62 miles) in Eco mode.

There’s also a fresh charger that Vespa says reduces energy consumption from the wall by 17%, with a 0-80% charge taking around 2.5 hours. A new Maintenance mode is designed to protect the battery during longer periods when the scooter isn’t being ridden.

Vespa is clearly only really interested in selling their gas models, which come in 50cc, 125cc, & 310cc classes. And the only reason anyone would get a 50cc is if they didn't want to bother to get an actual motorcycle license in some jurisdictions. The electrics are nearly as expensive as the 310s but even the "faster" model only has the power equivalent of about 70cc's. At least the battery in the faster model is now a decent 4.2 kwh, though that one I believe is not removable. Hey I'm actually a Vespa lover I have a 200cc. They are beautiful quality machines, and I don't mind the price premium. But the electrics are quite disappointing, especially for the money. If they had a true 125cc equivalent I would be first in line at the showroom. Very disappointing in that a stouter motor really wouldn't cost them much more at all.

The Primavera Tech also gets the technological bells and whistles you’d expect from the flagship version, including a 5-inch TFT display, keyless operation, navigation through Vespa’s smartphone connectivity system, and remote seat unlocking.

Perhaps the most Vespa thing about the whole patch is how little of it you can actually see.

Recent findings suggest that the company hasn’t tried to turn its electric scooters into rolling science-fiction props. They’re still unmistakably Vespas, complete with the same classic styling that has defined the brand for generations. They just happen to have a much more interesting electric drivetrain hiding underneath now.

Recent findings suggest that of course, they also carry some very Vespa pricing. While we don’t have word on the updated pricing for the new models, the outgoing Primavera Elettrica 70 RED was priced at $8,299 in the US. So don’t expect these models to come cheap.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A sprawling living room might be the dream, but having a small space doesn’t preclude you from being able to stretch out on the couch.
  • Sources indicate that being mindful of a space’s dimensions is always crucial when shopping for furniture, but especially so with a small room, where every inch may matter.
  • According to recent reports, the best-selling Abisko sectional from Article is made even more beautiful by colorful, performance velvet upholstery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A sprawling living room might be the dream, but having a small space doesn’t preclude you from being able to stretch out on the couch. Sectionals specifically designed for smaller rooms prove that cozy movie nights and afternoon naps aren’t reserved exclusively for those with a massive floor blueprint. In fact, choosing a sectional with the right proportions stands to make a smaller room feel larger. There’s no reason to settle for a hodgepodge of chairs and ottomans when a thoughtfully selected sectional can transform every seat into the best seat in the house.

Sources indicate that being mindful of a space’s dimensions is always crucial when shopping for furniture, but especially so with a small room, where every inch may matter. Still, a variety of clever configurations—including L-shaped sectionals designed to nestle into corners, modular designs that are easily rearranged, and sofas with reversible chaises that give you more flexibility—cater to seemingly every layout. Add in performance fabrics, washable slipcovers, and supportive cushions, and you’ve got a recipe for some seriously comfortable yet compact lounging. Ahead, we’re sharing our favorite sectionals for small spaces that ensure every square foot counts.

According to recent reports, the best-selling Abisko sectional from Article is made even more beautiful by colorful, performance velvet upholstery. Suitable for those with little ones and pets running around, the fabric is non-absorptive, meaning spills and crumbs won’t stay embedded in its weave. Two orientations—chaise and L-shaped—allow you to Tetris its silhouette into your space as you see fit.

Sources indicate that instead of opting for a giant L-shaped sectional that will take up the entire room, aim for something with a smaller footprint. Available in performance fabric and three leg finishes, this sectional couch is ideal for a tiny living space and a major upgrade from a smaller loveseat thanks to the chaise addition. While not an official fold-out sleeper sofa, the back cushions flop back to give you enough space should you be inclined to nap. Contributor David Kaufman, who tested it out for us, calls it “a great starter sofa for a first home or apartment that you won’t have to send to a landfill when you’re ready to move.”.

Similar to the Thuma sectional contributor Evan Russum told us “feels solid and durable,” the Essential Sofa follows the brand’s signature simple-but-considered aesthetic with a minimalist silhouette,rounded cushions, and a grounded wooden base. Raised armrests add sculptural presence without overwhelming a small living room, while the detachable ottoman lets you switch between a left- or right-facing chaise—so everyone can have a turn on their favorite side of the sofa.

Not your average grey couch, AllModern’s Jossa sectional is minimalist in looks but generous on comfort, thanks to its dense foam padding that offers plenty of support without feeling stiff. Easy to de-assemble, the modular design allows the sofa to evolve with your seating needs. Craving two separate lounge chairs? Done. Prefer a love seat? Just slide the two larger seats side-by-side. Today’s layout doesn’t have to be tomorrow’s.

The slim arms and low profile on this this reversible three-piece sectional make the Unwind especially suitable for a limited living area as it doesn’t monopolize the space. Five neutral color variations all come in a linen blend, but olive’s grounding tones are speaking most to us. This sectional, like many of the others on this list, can be configured to be left-facing or right-facing depending on your living room setup, and we particularly like that in case you tend to switch up your design layout (we certainly do).

Recent findings suggest that at just 62 inches wide, Sabai’s Essential Loveseat Sectional demonstrates how even the smallest living rooms can accommodate a proper chaise lounge. The compact design features clean lines, a generously sized chaise, and supportive foam cushions, offering the ideal spot to stretch out after a long day. Adding to the sectional’s appeal is its focus on sustainability. It combines a frame made from wood certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC)—a third-party verification that ensures ethical wood sourcing—with upholstery fashioned from recycled natural materials. It’s also easy to clean and maintain, largely thanks to its washable slipcovers, sold separately—a welcome feature for anyone whose couch often doubles as a dining chair for meals eaten over the coffee table. Suffice it to say, this sectional is particularly well-suited to apartment living.

Sources indicate that CB2’s Deseo sectional brings a little drama to small-space living, courtesy of rich, praline-brown performance velvet, broad arms, and a low-slung silhouette that practically begs you to sink in and stay awhile. The three-piece configuration, matching ottoman, and option for an extra-deep seat only extend the lounging possibilities and allow you to take advantage of every inch of your space. If brown doesn’t fit your space’s palette, worry not; the Deseo comes in plenty of other glamorous colors, including seven other performance velvet upholstery options.

It has been revealed that serious lounging is the goal for Sundays’ Movie Night sectional, with oversized cushions, deep seats, and a relaxed silhouette that makes it difficult to resist the urge to spend the afternoon totally horizontal. The cream linen upholstery adds to its laid-back feel, while the movable ottoman lets you stretch out or create a more open seating arrangement when organization comes over. The company’s own LiveLife performance fabric is stain-resistant, moisture-repellent, and washable, with removable slipcovers that make living with a light-colored sofa significantly less intimidating.

Recent findings suggest that interior Define takes customization very seriously, and the Sloan sectional showcases how having such options can pay off in a small living room. Choose your preferred upholstery, cushion fill, seat depth, and leg style, then fine-tune the dimensions to suit your floor plan. The reversible chaise adds another layer of flexibility, allowing you to change its orientation, in case you rearrange your furniture or move to a new place with a different layout.

Contributor Malia Griggs tested the Sloan in her own 196-square-foot living room, where she found that its supportive cushions, tailored silhouette, and carefully selected dimensions worked beautifully alongside a narrow entryway. “If you enjoy tailoring your décor to your taste, are willing to pay a bit more for quality, and have the patience for a made-to-order process, this is a wonderful sectional—especially for a smaller space,” she added.

What Features Should I Look for in a Sectional for Small Living Rooms?

It has been revealed that modular furniture—any sectional that comes in several parts so you can adjust your sofa to suit the configurations—is built with flexibility in mind, making it the ideal contender for a small living space. We have tested and loved Castlery modular sofas, but a search for modular sectional should give you plenty of other options. A room tight on space can benefit from couches with storage, like those from Albany Park. Now you’ll be able to minimize the clutter and extra blankets by stowing them underneath your seat.

How Do I Arrange a Sectional in a Small Space?

Sources indicate that don’t fall for the tiniest sectional you can find, but rather invest in something well-made—it plays a massive part in your living room, after all. While it may seem counterintuitive, Nashville interior designer Amanda Khouri says, “Filling a small room with small furniture can make it feel…well, smaller.”.

Designer Alicia Murphy used a sectional in the living room of a teensy trailer she converted into a plush family getaway in Montauk, Fresh York, for this very reason: “If you use a corner sectional rather than a sofa and chair, you most likely will add seating for two or three more people,” Murphy explains, noting that the alternative prevents you from having about 36 inches of dead space in the corner.”.

Another way to make it work? Set an L-shaped sectional across from two club chairs to create a conversation zone, advises interior designer Suzanne Dawson.

What Do I Look for in a High-Quality Sectional?

When you’re working with a small space, quality counts. It’s much harder to get away with a mid-century modern knock-off when it’s one of four furniture pieces packed into the room. When shopping for a sectional, evaluate the materials and care instructions. Avoid anything with plywood, and polyester when you can. Seek out solid wood construction, such as walnut, oak, or teak; and premium fabrics, like linen, leather, or chenille. You’ll also want to keep the warranty and return policy in mind, in case you want to send back a piece that doesn’t work for you.

  • Recent findings suggest that weighted blankets are a force in the sleep world, with fans swearing they can do everything from easing anxiety to helping you sleep better.
  • Still, if you’ve spent any amount of time wrapped in a weighted blanket, you know how cozy it can feel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that weighted blankets are a force in the sleep world, with fans swearing they can do everything from easing anxiety to helping you sleep better. While there are some small studies to support those claims, the science is still catching up.

Still, if you’ve spent any amount of time wrapped in a weighted blanket, you know how cozy it can feel. You’re basically in a cocoon, protected from the outside world. That extra weight also means this blanket won’t just slide off during the night, keeping you nice and snug all night long.

How do they work, you ask? The concept is pretty simple: These types of blankets mimic healing touch—something that reduces cortisol (the stress hormone) and boosts oxytocin (the feel-good hormone), Heidi Hanna, PhD, author of Stressaholic and an advisory board member for the American Institute of Stress, explains.

“While there isn’t much research to verify, the theory is that a weighted blanket works much like a hug,” adds Leisha Cuddihy, PhD, a clinical psychologist in behavioral sleep medicine. Hugging lowers blood pressure and stress hormones, which she says can help you snooze soundly. So, if you’re looking for some much-needed relief in the p.m., a weighted blanket is worth a try. Weighted blankets also make excellent holiday presents—who doesn’t want the gift of sleep?

In a recent development, not all weighted blankets are created equal, though. Fill, material, and the actual weight of the blanket matter.

Industry observers note that the most Instagrammable beauty of the bunch, Bearaby’s chunky weighted blanket is hand-knitted with layers of responsibly farmed organic cotton. Plus, since it doesn’t have fillers that pack in warmth, you’ll stay cozy without melting into a sweaty puddle overnight.

Sources indicate that WH social media editor Alyssa Cruz slept with this blanket for a month and notes it feels “just right” at night. “I absolutely love this blanket,” she shares, adding that the Bearaby blanket has improved her quality of sleep. “It is extremely comforting, and I find myself falling asleep within minutes,” she says. The blanket is so popular that Cruz and her roommate have taken turns sleeping with it. “The only cons is the size,” Cruz says. “You definitely have to be strategic with how you place it on your body, because it is very rectangular.” (Bearaby offers three different weights and sizes, giving you options to work with.) But Cruz says she’s still hooked. “I love it, and would buy ten more if I could.”.

Make way for the OG. This weighted blanket made its debut in 2017, following the makers’ successful $5 million Kickstarter campaign to fund production. Gridded stitching on the blanket ensures that glass beads are distributed evenly, reaching every pressure point. Plus, we love the velvety flannel material for colder months.

Gravity has a smart design that makes this blanket easy to care for: Just remove the outside cover and toss it in the washing machine. (The inner blanket is hand wash only.) If you tend to run hot, this isn’t the blanket for you—it can get pretty toasty at night. But if you’re on the hunt for a snuggly weighted blanket that’s convenient and comfortable, give this one a go.

According to recent reports, weighted blankets tend to be pricey, with some costing upwards of $200. But the ZZZhen weighted blanket is just $30, making it accessible to most people. The blanket has a smooth exterior and internal grid system that’s designed to keep the interior glass beads in place.

Sources indicate that this blanket does the trick, delivering that classic warm hug feeling people crave in a weighted blanket. It’s also soft, and machine washable, making it easy to care for. We like that it comes in a 7-pound size, giving people newly introduced to weighted blankets a lighter-weight option if they want to ease in.

Industry observers note that of course, there are a few sacrifices to consider while you’re saving money. It’s unclear what the blanket is made from—some descriptions say cotton, while others say polyester. The sizing also tends to run a little small. But you can still get a lot for $30 with this option.

Weighted blankets take a little more thought than regular blankets. You have to figure out a weight that’s best for your needs, along with choosing a color that fits your decor. While many weighted blanket companies limit you to two or three weight options, YnM allows you to pick from 11 choices, along with 22 shades, giving you plenty of room for customization.

The blanket is made from a lightweight cotton for a surprisingly breezy feel. Available in weights from 7 to 50 pounds, the blanket is composed of seven layers that snugly envelop your every curve. But its largest size is 88” by 104”, allowing you to share it with a partner.

According to recent reports, available in three, eight, and 10-pound options, the Lola Weighted Blanket is great for anyone who wants some heft without feeling too heavy. The double-sided OEKO-TEX Standard 100-certified faux fur is unbelievably silky-soft, plus Its stain-resistant and sheds zero.

Recent findings suggest that “It kept me warm and cozy without being overwhelming because of the extra weight,” says WH social media producer Rianna Cafaro. “It was just right.” While some weighted blankets look utilitarian, that’s not the case with the Lola blanket. It’s fuzzy exterior makes it incredibly inviting. While Cafaro didn’t notice any drawbacks of this blanket during testing, she did point out that it’s pricey. Still, she says, “it is worth the price.”.

Straying from the pack, Layla’s blanket is available in only one weight, depending on your mattress size. But that means it’s enough for you and your bedmate to share (score!). The top layer is plush, while the other feels like a cool cotton bedsheet.

WH fitness and reviews editor Natascha Grief loved the fabric options, especially the plush side. “It kind of feels like being hugged by a stuffed animal,” she says. Grief says that the blanket delivers a comforting feel without the bulk. “The fill was silent and virtually unnoticeable,” she says. “It didn't shift around every time I did.” Grief also says she didn’t notice any uncomfortable pressure points like she has in the past as a side sleeper with other weighted blankets.

In a recent development, the only downside, per Grief, is that this only comes in one color (black). While you can toss the whole thing in the wash, just be aware of your machine’s capacity. Larger sizes may be tough to stuff into a compact washer.

There’s a wide range of textures with weighted blankets—some have a stuffed animal-like feel, while others are more functional. The Baloo weighted blanket falls into the second camp, with a comforter style design you can toss on your bed and leave there.

Recent findings suggest that WH entertainment editor Amy Wilkinson praises the temperature regulation of this blanket, noting that it felt just right. It’s on the thinner side, but is great for layering and all-season use, she points out—just add on another layer in the winter and take one off in the summer. “The 15-pound weight felt just right for getting the soothing compression of a weighted blanket without feeling like you’re being squished in your sleep,” Wilkinson claims. Just be aware that you may need to size up. Wilkinson got a full/queen size and found that it didn’t cover her entire queen bed. Still, she says, “as a no-frills comforter, it does the job.”.

It’s no surprise that this is the most vital consideration. There’s no one perfect weight. Rather, it’s essential to get a blanket that’s right for your body type. Weighted blankets typically range from 5 to 30 pounds, and many experts suggest picking one that’s around 10 percent of your body weight. This will ensure you don’t experience any discomfort as you sleep. Ideally, you want the right amount of pressure without putting so much weight on your body that you feel “trapped” or suffocated.

According to recent reports, you’ll want a blanket that offers uniform pressure to feel the calming effect, says Cuddihy. Look for quality stitching, layers of material, and glass-bead fill. Some lower-quality weighted blankets will have plastic pellets instead of glass beads, so keep an eye out when shopping.

Recent findings suggest that depending on the time of year and whether you run hot or cold, the material your weighted blanket is made from matters. If you’re a hot sleeper, look for blankets made with breathable fabrics like bamboo or cotton. A removable cover can be helpful, too, for easier machine washing. If you like to be bundled in warmth under your blankets, look for materials like fleece or microfiber.

It has been revealed that weighted blankets need to be washed, too, making it key to find one that won’t make your life harder. Blankets filled with glass microbeads, plastic pellets, steel beads, or pebbles can usually go in the wash, while those that are filled with organic materials often can’t. Your washing machine may also not be able to handle the extra weight. So, read the care instructions before purchasing your blanket to make sure it lines up with your lifestyle.

Sources indicate that there’s a lot of variety with weighted blanket sizing, making it important to read the measurements carefully. If you strategy to use your weighted blanket on your bed like a comforter, or just want to make sure it’ll cover your body while you snooze, try measuring out the size on your bed to see what it will look like to get a better sense. Consider sizing up if you’re unsure.

Our editors regularly test bedding, including weighted blankets, and they continue to try fresh products as they’re released. We last updated this story in March. Since then, we tested four additional weighted blankets for a month or more.

We spent many nights at home snuggled under weighted blankets comparing weight, texture, temperature regulation, size, and performance. Naturally, comfort was heavily weighed during testing. When testing, we also took into consideration which blankets were best for the sofa versus for actually sleeping under for the night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 70-year-old California woman who reportedly suffered serious injuries in a head-on collision with a Tesla Model Y in the Bay Area this summer has filed a lawsuit against the automaker, the driver, and the organizers of a nearby Cars & Coffee event.
  • Sources indicate that according to a civil complaint filed in San Mateo County Superior Court, a Tesla representative was demonstrating the vehicle's performance for event photographers.
  • Sources indicate that the incident occurred on August 30, 2026, according to the filing, along State Route 84 near La Honda, California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 70-year-old California woman who reportedly suffered serious injuries in a head-on collision with a Tesla Model Y in the Bay Area this summer has filed a lawsuit against the automaker, the driver, and the organizers of a nearby Cars & Coffee event.

Sources indicate that according to a civil complaint filed in San Mateo County Superior Court, a Tesla representative was demonstrating the vehicle's performance for event photographers. The driver allegedly reached speeds exceeding 80 miles per hour on a stretch of road with posted speed limits of 35–40 mph; the complaint claims he lost control on a blind curve, and crashed into Michelle Brooks's Honda CR-V.

Sources indicate that the incident occurred on August 30, 2026, according to the filing, along State Route 84 near La Honda, California. The lawsuit identifies the Tesla driver as 21-year-old Micah Zuglian, who was allegedly driving a organization-owned Model Y while attending a Cars & Coffee gathering at Ambassador Wine Garden. According to the complaint, Zuglian took two photographers associated with the event for a drive to demonstrate the Tesla's performance. Images allegedly captured during the drive show the vehicle's speedometer displaying 83 mph; another image reportedly demonstrates a speed of 61 mph near a posted 35-mph speed limit sign.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit alleges that Zuglian subsequently crossed the double-yellow lines on the road and struck Brooks's 2014 Honda CR-V head-on. Brooks had to be transported to Stanford Hospital for treatment of her injuries, which reportedly included fractured vertebrae, fractured ribs, broken limbs, and a traumatic brain injury.

It has been revealed that the complaint alleges that representatives from the California Highway Patrol, San Mateo County Sheriff's Office, and a county supervisor's office met with event organizers beforehand and urged them to cancel the gathering over traffic safety concerns. The suit claims that roads in the area are notorious for racing, and that in the past five years, more than 20 people have died and almost 800 have been injured in automobile crashes in the vicinity.

Brooks alleges that Tesla negligently entrusted the Model Y to its representative and failed to adequately supervise him. The complaint also alleges negligence by the event organizers for proceeding despite the reported safety concerns. The plaintiff is seeking damages and requesting a jury trial.

The lawsuit also names Ethan Garabedian, doing business as “9burgring,” which organized the gathering, and Ambassador Wine Bars LLC, which hosted it. The allegations have not been proven in court, and the filing of a lawsuit does not establish liability on the part of Tesla, Zuglian, or the event organizers.

Sources indicate that toyota now offers three fully electric SUVs: the bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland. Here’s how they stack up.

After introducing the newly introduced and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV quickly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.

In the first nine months of 2026, it was the fourth-best-selling electric vehicle, behind the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

With two additional electric SUVs now on sale, the CH-R and bZ Woodland, Toyota has suddenly become one of America’s top-selling EV brands.

Its EV sales have nearly tripled this year. According to Cox Automotive, Toyota ranked as the third most popular EV brand behind Tesla and Rivian in the third quarter.

Toyota offers three distinct electric vehicles: the 2027 bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland, each designed for different lifestyles, so which one is the best fit for you?

It has been revealed that after launching the updated model last year, the 2027 bZ starts at $34,980. With the $1,595 delivery fee, the starting price is $36,576.

Industry observers note that that’s for the standard 2027 Toyota bZ XLE FWD with an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 236 miles. For longer range, you can upgrade to the FWD Plus model, which offers up to 314 miles and starts at $37,980 (excluding the delivery fee).

The Toyota bZ is available in XLE and Limited grades, with front- or all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrains.

Two battery options are offered: The 57.7 kWh battery on the standard XLE FWD provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 236 miles, while the larger 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 288 miles of range on the XLE AWD and 314 miles on the XLE FWD Plus model.

FWD models produce either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models deliver a combined 338 hp.

It has been revealed that the 2027 bZ also has a built-in NACS port, so you can use Tesla Superchargers without needing a separate adapter. Toyota stated it takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

Industry observers note that inside, the 2027 bZ features Toyota’s updated cabin design. The setup features a 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and a new 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The bZ is essentially designed as an everyday driver with a long driving range, modern tech, and available AWD.

For those looking for a bigger, more rugged option, the 2027 bZ Woodland may be a better fit. The Woodland is 6″ longer than the standard bZ and comes with standard AWD.

The longer body opens up more interior space, with up to 74.3 cubic feet of storage compared to the bZ with up to 67.1 cubic feet.

Unlike the bZ, the Woodland model has a standard AWD powertrain with Toyota’s X-Mode control system.

The setup delivers a combined 375 horsepower, 37 hp more than the standard bZ, making it Toyota’s most powerful EV currently.

It also adopts a more commanding, upright stance with 8.3″ of ground clearance and 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Sources indicate that although it uses the same 74.7 kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland’s EPA-estimated range drops to 281 miles because of the added weight and power. Upgrading to the optional all-terrain tires sacrifices even more range, with up to 260 miles.

Sources indicate that like the bZ, the Woodland also has a built- in NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes around 30 minutes.

Inside, the bZ Woodland features the same 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380. All variants include standard roof rails, Dual Qi-capable wireless device chargers, heated front seats and steering wheel, and Digital Key capabilities.

Last, but not least, the C-HR is a smaller, sporty, coupe-like electric SUV. The 2027 Toyota C-HR starts at $37,080, or $2,100 more than the standard bZ.

It has been revealed that it’s about 6.7″ shorter than the bZ, with a smaller wheelbase, but also comes with standard AWD. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 338 hp, not quite as much as the bigger, more powerful Woodland.

The C-HR is available exclusively with the 74.7 kWh battery, which provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 287 miles for the SE grade with 18″ wheels.

Upgrading to 20″ wheels adds a street-ready look but offers slightly less EPA range, with up to 273 miles.

The coupe-like design adds a sleek look and opens up interior space, with up to 59.5 cubic feet of rear cargo space when the rear seats are folded. That’s slightly more than the bZ, which offers up to 56.9 cubic feet.

Inside, the C-HR features the same setup as its other EVs, including a 7″ slim driver’s display and 14″ central infotainment screen.

Sources indicate that like Toyota’s other electric SUVs, the C-HR has a native NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes.

According to recent reports, these are all basically the same small vehicles. I did not fit in any of them (6’ 2”) it is so frustrating to have less than 300 miles of range on AWD versions that are supposed to be better models.

It is 2026 over a decade since EVs arrived and over 5 years after the Tesla Model Y with practically zero competition almost at same price (Rivian R2 may be next year when affordable versions ship.) BMW, Mercedes and Volvo need $10k more. Hyundai has kept EV5 out of USA.

It is almost like none of the Legacy automakers want any SUV that can compete on price.

The 2027 Toyota C-HR EV is available in two trims: SE and XSE. Standard features include two wireless Qi phone chargers, low-profile roof rails, Fabric/SofTex-trimmed seating, heated front seats and steering wheel, Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, and a power liftgate.

Solid–liquid mixing, where particles are dispersed in a liquid, is essential in many industrial processes such as slurry preparation, crystallization, precipitation, adsorption and dissolution. In such cases, effective mixing is critical for contact between particles and liquid, enabling mass transfer. With only three key factors to keep in mind, shopping for at-home waxing kits is refreshingly simple.

Before waxing, you should know there are two types of waxes: hard and soft.

According to recent reports, if you want to use something stripless, go for hard wax. It adheres to the hair follicle (versus the skin), hardens, and can be removed on its own, eliminating the need for paper strips. For some, it may even feel less painful than soft wax, so it's great for sensitive skin, says dermatologist Nazanin Saedi, MD. The only caveat is that you may have to apply it several times in the same area to make sure all the hairs you target are removed.

In a recent development, soft wax, on the other hand, is soft and applied in a thin layer. A paper strip is then used to adhere and remove the wax. Often, the top layer of skin is also removed, so it can be irritating for people with sensitive skin.

Ideally, beginners should look for kits that contain everything they need to get the job done—wax, strips, and finishing oil, at minimum. Novices may also appreciate waxing kits that come with pre-loaded strips, since they're less messy and require less precision. The tradeoff? You're limited to the size of the included strips, so look for kits with multiple sizes if you're targeting different areas of the body. Larger strips are fantastic for your legs, while small strips are practical for your face.

It's key to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin. If you have sensitive skin, look for waxing kits that include skin-soothing ingredients, like castor and almond oils or aloe. And whatever you use, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. This will allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

Recent findings suggest that for the past year, Women’s Health contributors and I, including Sabrina Talbert, Jasmine Gomez, Danielle Jackson, and Cristina Montemayor, tested the bestselling, most popular, and top-rated at-home waxing kits. Our team consulted dermatologists Blair Murphy-Rose, MD, Nazanin Saedi, MD, and Uchenna Okereke, MD, for pre-waxing advice and aftercare instructions to prevent irritation and promote healthy skin. Then, we got our hands on the kits and tested them in the comfort of our own homes, evaluating attributes like ease of use, comfort, results, and overall value. Of the 25 at-home waxing kits tested, the seven on this list delivered the best results in our in-depth evaluations.

Industry observers note that at-home waxing removes body hair conveniently and cost-effectively, and the best kits do it swiftly while minimizing pain and irritation. So, if you’re ready to ditch the razors, check out this list of the best waxing kits, tested by dermatologists and WH editors.

Sources indicate that after waxing, you can prevent ingrown hairs from forming and minimize irritation immediately afterward by applying cool aloe to soothe skin, and sticking to loose clothes that won't create friction. "Aloe vera has anti-inflammatory properties that help soothe sunburned skin, while glycerin specifically can help to boost hydration levels to restore the skin's moisture barrier," dermatologist Divya Shokeen, MD, previously told WH in our guide to the best aloe vera gel. Some kits also come with nourishing oils and wipes to help minimize any post-wax irritation.

Before you head off to wax unwanted hair, these are a few other tips you should keep in mind.

Waxing removes hair by lifting it out at the root. With traditional waxing, hot wax is applied to skin and the hair is pulled off in the opposite direction of the way it's growing. The key word here and what can make at-home waxing dangerous is that it's hot.

“Hot wax can burn the skin—and it is a particularly dangerous type of burn because the hot product adheres to the skin,” states Dr. Murphy-Rose. Always make sure you're following the heating directions closely and that you hold your hand over the wax after it's been heated to gauge the temperature before applying it to your skin.

Recent findings suggest that then, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. "That way you can check the temperature, but also see how your skin reacts," indicates Dr. Saedi. Testing a product will also allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. “It's important to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin," says Dr. Murphy-Rose. You should also avoid any ingredients you have a known allergy or sensitivity to. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

It has been revealed that "Hot wax tends to adhere the strongest, so while it may remove hairs more efficiently, it can also stick to skin more and pull off those top layers of the skin as it's also pulling out your hair,” says Dr. Murphy-Rose.

Industry observers note that waxing exfoliates the top layer of skin and is more likely to cause hyperpigmentation a.k.a. dark spots, indicates Dr. Okereke. She says to think of the skin after waxing like a fresh, pink wound. "Ultraviolet rays are attracted to wounds, making the freshly waxed skin more susceptible to darkening as melanin (the dark pigment in skin) floods the area to try and protect it." Luckily, there is a simple fix: Wear broad-spectrum sunscreen! Better yet, keep that new skin out of the sun completely for at least a few days.

According to recent reports, you'll also want to avoid any extra exfoliation, like retinol, chemical peels, and microdermabrasion, a few days prior and a few days following your at-home wax. A few other good things to know before getting started: Always wax on clean skin to avoid bacterial contamination in pores and make sure your hairs are long enough (at least 1/4 of an inch) to be grabbed by the wax.

The key to preventing ingrown hairs (an all too common downside of waxing for many) is to get the full hair follicle. The best way to do this is by keeping your skin taut and pulling the wax strip in the opposite direction of the way that your hair grows.

In a recent development, sugaring, aka sugared wax or sugar gel, is generally safer because it’s applied to skin at room temperature (read: no risk of burning skin) and warms up with body heat. “Sugared ‘wax’ is not truly wax,” Dr. Murphy-Rose notes. Rather, it’s a combination of sugar, lemon juice, and water. Some brands will infuse glycerin, fragrance, honey, or essential oils. Regardless of which brand you opt for, sugaring is water-soluble and easily rinses off the skin compared to hot wax, she says.

Industry observers note that sugaring and threading remove the hair follicle from the root but with less exfoliating, offering a gentler process, Dr. Okereke says. Though she warns that she's also had patients with coily-textured hair that still develop ingrown hairs and scarring from sugaring as well. The bottom line: "If you know you're prone to hyperpigmentation, ingrown hairs, or scarring, see a dermatologist to discuss the best hair removal practices for you," says Dr. Okereke.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The upcoming Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.
  • Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan, including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.
  • The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The upcoming Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.

Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan, including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.

The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.

According to recent reports, while that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.

Sources indicate that the EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.

During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.

Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.

Both beat the older EQS, which reached a peak charge rate of 208 kW and sustained an average of 175 kW.

The fresh Mercedes EQS 450+ added 825 miles of range in an hour, and 100 miles in just over 7 minutes, nearly twice the speed of the 2025MY.

The Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions. It includes 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

Industry observers note that how much is too much? 539 miles on a single charge is impressive, but do you need it? In a recent “nationally representative” survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

Industry observers note that the study showed that 73% consider 25, 50, or 75 miles enough to cover their daily driving. However, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range before they would consider an EV.

If you have access to a home charger, nothing beats waking up with a full charge every day. Meanwhile, public charging continues to improve, giving EV drivers more reliable options on longer trips.

According to recent reports, faster charging also helps. Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in around 10 minutes.

It has been revealed that in the same Edmunds EV Range Test last week, the newly introduced 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, exceeding its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. It also used 28.3 kWh per 100 miles during the test, beating its official EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles.

I'm really glad to see more articles like this and people talking more about efficiency. It's not just about bigger batteries and range. It needs to be about smaller batteries plus great efficiency giving that same range. We need to do this with more efficient designs, more sedans and lighter vehicles.

The latest 2027 Volvo EX60 drove 352 miles while the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric covered 392 miles during the same test.

Sources indicate that one thing is certain: electric vehicles are becoming more efficient, enabling longer driving ranges and faster charging times. As battery tech advances, EVs will drive farther and charge faster, while safety and performance will continue to improve.

Sources indicate that how much driving range would you consider enough for your daily drive? What about for the week? Let us know in the comments below.

It has been revealed that plugShare is giving its EV charging app a significant overhaul. Version 8.0 arrives worldwide for iPhone on November 10, with dark mode, a trip planner that shows how far apart charging stops are, and a rebuilt Apple Watch app that can point you to a charger compatible with your EV.

It has been revealed that dark mode was one of the most-requested features from PlugShare owners. It works across the app and follows your iPhone’s settings, so if your phone switches to dark mode at sunset, your charging map will, too.

It has been revealed that the trip planner gets a small but handy change. Each charging stop now shows how far it is from both the start of your trip and the previous stop. So when you’re deciding whether to stretch to the next fast charger or stop sooner, the number you need is right there.

#40991. Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1087 w)
